nodes.title: SG-4 · Integrate Phaser 3.90 with a lifecycle-safe React host and typed events
nodes.body: Context: game/frontend is a React 18 + Vite + zustand app. SceneView.tsx renders the bedroom as an plus absolutely positioned hotspot buttons. useGame.ts keeps GameState in React useState, and uiStore.ts holds only UI flags. Phaser is not installed and no src/phaser folder exists. Desired behavior: install Phaser 3.90 and add a PhaserHost React component that owns exactly one Phaser.Game, with pixel-art config, resize and device-pixel-ratio handling. Add a typed event bus for Phaser to React and React to Phaser messages. Move shared GameState into a Zustand store that Phaser reads without duplicating it. Expected result: unit tests with Phaser mocked prove single-instance creation, cleanup on unmount, resize handling and typed event delivery. Why: it is the base for the layered Phaser scene work in later sub-goals. ## Acceptance criteria - Given package.json, When dependencies are read, Then phaser resolves to a 3.90.x version. - Given PhaserHost mounts under React.StrictMode, When effects run twice, Then the Phaser game factory returns exactly one live instance and destroys the first before the second is created. - Given PhaserHost unmounts, When cleanup runs, Then game.destroy(true) is called once and no instance remains. - Given the game config, When it is built, Then pixelArt and roundPixels are true and scale mode is FIT with integer-friendly zoom. - Given a typed event is emitted on the bus, When a listener is subscribed, Then the listener receives the exact typed payload and no payload after unsubscribe. - Given GameState changes in the Zustand store, When a Phaser scene reads it, Then it gets the store value and keeps no copy. ## Scope - In scope: phaser dependency - In scope: PhaserHost component - In scope: pixel-art game config and scale helper - In scope: typed event bus - In scope: Zustand game store read by a Phaser scene - In scope: unit tests with Phaser mocked - Out of scope: layered bedroom rendering - Out of scope: sprites and animations - Out of scope: Go backend changes - Out of scope: replacing SceneView in App - Preserve: useGame return shape: state, scene, view, act, choose - Preserve: existing tests under game/frontend/tests - Preserve: localStorage persistence behavior ## Technical constraints - Phaser 3.90 - TypeScript - Zustand for shared state - Tests under game/frontend/tests, run with vitest run - Unit tests must mock the phaser module ## Definition of done - All requirements delivered with Act and Verify units - Unit tests pass and tsc --noEmit passes ## Non-functional requirements - No duplicate Phaser instances or listener leaks ## Clarifying questions - None

nodes.title: REQ · PhaserHost creates one pixel-art Phaser 3.90 game, handles resize and destroys it on unmount
nodes.body:
Context: Phaser is absent from game/frontend. Desired behavior: add phaser ^3.90.0, a createGame factory wrapping new Phaser.Game(config), a config builder with pixelArt, roundPixels, FIT scaling with integer zoom, and a PhaserHost component guarded against StrictMode double-mount. A ResizeObserver on the container refreshes scaling for container size and devicePixelRatio. Expected result: one live game instance, destroyed on unmount. Why: prevents leaked canvases and blurry scaling.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given PhaserHost mounts in StrictMode, When effects run mount, cleanup, mount, Then at most one game is alive and destroy(true) was called on the first.
- Given PhaserHost unmounts, When cleanup runs, Then destroy(true) is called and the ref is null.
- Given buildGameConfig is called, When read, Then render.pixelArt and render.roundPixels are true and scale.mode is FIT.
- Given a container of 1000x600 at DPR 2, When computeZoom runs with a 640x360 logical size, Then it returns an integer of at least 1.
- Given the observed container resizes, When the observer fires, Then game.scale.refresh is called.


## Scope
- In scope: phaser dependency
- In scope: createGame factory
- In scope: buildGameConfig and computeZoom
- In scope: PhaserHost component
- Out of scope: scene content
- Out of scope: event bus
- Preserve: existing components and tests


## Technical constraints
- Phaser 3.90
- Zoom is an integer


## Dependencies
- INT


## Definition of done
- PhaserHost, config and factory exist and typecheck


## Non-functional requirements
- No leaked canvas elements


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · A typed event bus defines Phaser to React and React to Phaser events
nodes.body:
Context: no bridge exists between Phaser and React. Desired behavior: create src/phaser/events.ts with PhaserToReactEvents (objectHover {id: string|null}, objectClick {id: string}, sceneReady {sceneId: string}) and ReactToPhaserEvents (highlightObject {id: string|null}, playAnimation {target: string, name: string}, transitionTo {sceneId: string}). Provide createEventBus<T>() with on (returning unsubscribe), off, emit and clear, and two exported buses. Expected result: typed delivery with no Phaser import. Why: React and Phaser need decoupled communication.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a listener on objectClick, When emit('objectClick', {id:'bookshelf'}) runs, Then the listener receives {id:'bookshelf'} once.
- Given the unsubscribe returned by on is called, When emit runs again, Then the listener is not called.
- Given clear() is called, When any event is emitted, Then no listener is called.
- Given the events module, When it is imported, Then it does not import phaser.


## Scope
- In scope: createEventBus
- In scope: two event maps
- In scope: exported buses
- Out of scope: wiring into scenes
- Preserve: existing store


## Technical constraints
- TypeScript generics keyed by event map
- No Phaser import in events.ts


## Dependencies
- INT


## Definition of done
- events.ts typechecks with generic event maps


## Non-functional requirements
- No listener leaks after unsubscribe


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Phaser reads shared GameState from a Zustand store without duplicating it
nodes.body:
Context: useGame.ts holds GameState in useState, which Phaser cannot read. Desired behavior: add src/store/gameStore.ts exporting useGameStore with state: GameState|null and setState(updater). useGame reads and writes this store while keeping its return shape and localStorage persistence. Add src/phaser/BootScene.ts, a Phaser.Scene that reads useGameStore.getState().state on demand, subscribes to store changes and emits sceneReady, without keeping its own copy. Expected result: one owner of state. Why: avoids duplicated state ownership.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the store is set to a GameState, When BootScene.readState() runs, Then it returns the store's object by reference.
- Given the store changes, When the BootScene subscription fires, Then the scene reads the new state and holds no cached copy.
- Given useGame renders, When act is called, Then the store state updates and the return shape is unchanged.
- Given BootScene shuts down, When shutdown runs, Then the store subscription is removed.


## Scope
- In scope: gameStore
- In scope: useGame refactor to the store
- In scope: BootScene state reading
- Out of scope: rendering sprites
- Preserve: useGame return shape
- Preserve: readSaved/writeSaved persistence
- Preserve: existing useGame tests


## Technical constraints
- Zustand ^5
- BootScene extends Phaser.Scene


## Dependencies
- INT
- REQ2


## Definition of done
- useGame uses the store and existing tests still pass


## Non-functional requirements
- Subscription removed on shutdown


## Clarifying questions
- None

steps.action: Add the dependency "phaser": "^3.90.0" to the dependencies object, then run npm install in game/frontend to update package-lock.json.
steps.expected: package.json lists phaser ^3.90.0 and node_modules/phaser/package.json version starts with 3.90.

steps.action: Create the file. Export GAME_WIDTH=640 and GAME_HEIGHT=360. Export computeZoom(w:number,h:number,dpr:number):number returning Math.max(1, Math.floor(Math.min(w*dpr/GAME_WIDTH, h*dpr/GAME_HEIGHT))). Export buildGameConfig(parent:HTMLElement, scenes: Phaser.Types.Scenes.SceneType[]): Phaser.Types.Core.GameConfig with type Phaser.AUTO, parent, width GAME_WIDTH, height GAME_HEIGHT, render {pixelArt:true, roundPixels:true, antialias:false}, scale {mode: Phaser.Scale.FIT, autoCenter: Phaser.Scale.CENTER_BOTH}, scene scenes.
steps.expected: buildGameConfig returns a config with render.pixelArt true and scale.mode Phaser.Scale.FIT.

steps.action: Create the file exporting createGame(parent:HTMLElement, scenes): Phaser.Game that returns new Phaser.Game(buildGameConfig(parent, scenes)). This is the single seam tests mock.
steps.expected: createGame is the only place new Phaser.Game is called.

steps.action: Create PhaserHost with props {scenes?: Phaser.Types.Scenes.SceneType[]}. Use containerRef (div) and gameRef (useRef<Phaser.Game|null>(null)). In a useEffect with [] deps: if gameRef.current is null and containerRef.current exists, set gameRef.current = createGame(containerRef.current, scenes ?? []). Create a ResizeObserver on the container whose callback calls gameRef.current?.scale.refresh(). The cleanup disconnects the observer, calls gameRef.current?.destroy(true), and sets gameRef.current = null. Render <div ref={containerRef} className="h-full w-full" data-testid="phaser-host" />.
steps.expected: Mounting creates one game, unmounting destroys it and nulls the ref.

nodes.summary: Store GameState in Zustand; BootScene reads it without copying.
nodes.description: Create gameStore, refactor useGame to use it and add a Phaser scene that reads from it.
acceptance_criteria: Given useGame, When read, Then state comes from useGameStore.
Given BootScene, When read, Then it keeps no GameState field.

steps.action: Create a zustand store with interface GameStoreState {state: GameState | null; setState: (updater: (prev: GameState) => GameState) => void; init: (s: GameState) => void}. init sets state only when state is null; setState applies updater to the current non-null state.
steps.code:
import { create } from 'zustand';
import type { GameState } from '@game/state/types';
steps.expected: useGameStore.getState().state is null until init is called.

steps.action: Remove the useState call. Compute the initial value readSaved() ?? createInitialState(world, scene) and call useGameStore.getState().init(initial) before reading. Select state with useGameStore((s)=>s.state) as GameState. Keep the writeSaved useEffect on state. Change act to useGameStore.getState().setState((prev)=>performAction(prev, scene, objectId, actionId)) and choose to the equivalent with chooseOption. Keep the return object keys unchanged.
steps.code: before: setState((prev) => performAction(...)) -> after: useGameStore.getState().setState((prev) => performAction(prev, scene, objectId, actionId))
steps.expected: useGame returns the same keys and updates through the store.

steps.action: Create class BootScene extends Phaser.Scene with constructor super('BootScene'), private unsubscribe: (() => void) | null = null (not state), readState(): GameState | null returning useGameStore.getState().state, create() that subscribes with this.unsubscribe = useGameStore.subscribe(() => this.onStateChange()) and emits phaserToReact.emit('sceneReady',{sceneId:'boot'}), onStateChange() that calls this.readState(), and in create registers this.events.once(Phaser.Scenes.Events.SHUTDOWN, () => {this.unsubscribe?.(); this.unsubscribe = null;}).
steps.expected: BootScene never stores a GameState field and unsubscribes on shutdown.
